title: Add the one-paragraph data notice to the intake form and the invitation, and record the policy identifier 'none: internal cohort, D-M' on every cohort decision
description: Why: the council of 2026-10-23 (030 Q8, D-51) decided the internal cohort is not candidate-impacting selection but is still people with rights, so a plain data notice is not deferred: what is collected, who sees it, that no model reads it and no link is fetched, how to withdraw and how to request erasure, as one approved paragraph on the intake form (the same form invitation mode serves) and in the invitation mail. Every qualification decision for the cohort records the policy identifier 'none: internal cohort, D-M' so 019 section 6's never-rewritten history can tell these cases apart later. The notice wording is approved by the owner with the templates (211.7.7); the mechanism is repo-only. Authority: repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: the launch manifest and the first internal journey.
acceptance_criteria: The intake form and the invitation render the approved notice paragraph from one template with a recorded version and hash; a test proves the notice is present on the request-access page in invitation mode and in the invitation mail body; a cohort decision stores the policy identifier 'none: internal cohort, D-M' and the 019 section 6 history shows it; the wording is a template the owner approves, not a constant.
notes: Roles: implementer Claude Code (repo-only); reviewer catalyst-security-privacy (the notice) and catalyst-django-operator (the decision form); approver: the owner (wording with 211.7.7).

title: Bound the unbounded waits with an aged-waits health part and page thresholds, so a stalled case is noticed without an owner mail notice
description: Outcome: with the first-generation owner notices retired, a stalled wait is still seen. Found by the operator and correspondence reviews of 2026-10-23: the health report has no stage-based part, open staff items report an oldest age but raise no anomaly, and a sent agreement awaiting signature, a reply awaiting staff processing, a provider-unavailable provisioning activation, an application awaiting decision or on hold, and a paused stack have no bound. Builds: one aged_waits part in the system health report counting applications in awaiting_decision, on_hold and assessing past a threshold, open staff items, pauses, replies awaiting processing and issued agreements (including the countersignature) past it, reusing the existing pending-age setting; anomaly codes only; the thresholds and whether each pages are the owner's values (211.7.2, 211.7.7). Non-goals: a new notification channel; any mail to the owner. Authority class: repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: release preparation. Evidence: CI tests; the health report in the dark deploy. Roles: implementer Claude Code in a released handoff; reviewer catalyst-django-operator and catalyst-workflow-correspondence; approver: the owner.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with aged fixtures: each listed wait past its threshold raises its anomaly code and clears when resolved; a fresh wait raises nothing; codes only, no identifiers; the report prints the oldest age per wait class.

title: Give an on-hold application a staff path back to a decision and give staff a verification resend, through the decision service
description: Outcome: two states that today need a shell get a supported staff path. Found by the operator review of 2026-10-23: an application on hold has no path back to a decision except closure (the decision service accepts only awaiting_decision and assessing as source stages), and no staff view or command can resend a verification challenge (a failed send is not retried). Builds: the hold-to-decision transition in the decision service under the existing direct-grant decision permission, with the stage machine and triggers updated; a staff resend of the verification challenge from the dossier under the correspondence staff permission, with the same uniform response and limits as issuance. Non-goals: a new workflow framework; any change to applicant-facing pages. Authority class: repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: release preparation. Evidence: CI tests. Roles: implementer Claude Code in a released handoff; reviewer catalyst-django-operator and catalyst-minimax-evaluation (the decision-service change); approver: the owner.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a decision-maker moves an on-hold case to a decision through the decision form and the transition is recorded with the permission checked and a refused attempt by a user without it; a staff member resends a verification challenge from the dossier, the old challenge is superseded, a resend is refused beyond the limit, and the applicant-facing response is unchanged; both walked in the 9kg.41 record.

title: Build the read-only Sent-folder evidence source and the production mail-host allow-list so an uncertain send can be reconciled live
description: Outcome: a send whose outcome is unknown can be settled against the provider, not only against the fake. Found by the correspondence review of 2026-10-23: no Sent-folder reader exists, the guards refuse a send-evidence source outside the test environment, and the mail-host guard refuses any non-loopback host and any environment outside development, test and staging, so the live reconcile that 029 section 5.2 relies on cannot run. Builds: a read-only IMAP Sent reader that enumerates by time window and matches on recipient and content digest (absence of a copy is not proof of non-send); an exact production mail-host allow-list read from configuration; the guard change that admits the production host for the web and worker roles only; codes-only records. Non-goals: any write to the mailbox; a second poller of the first-generation mailbox. Authority class: repo-only. Earliest boundary blocked: the mail canary and release preparation (mail is required at launch). Evidence: CI tests with the fake; the live proof is the mail canary. Roles: implementer Claude Code in a released handoff; reviewer catalyst-workflow-correspondence, then catalyst-security-privacy (the allow-list and guard); approver: the owner.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: an uncertain send is settled as sent when a matching Sent copy exists in the window, as not sent when none exists and the attempt is old, and stays a staff item when the folder cannot be read; the reader never writes; the allow-list refuses any host not named and refuses an empty list outside synthetic environments; the first-generation mailbox cannot be configured as a source; records carry codes only.

title: Owner decision: POL-09 custody storage location, access rules and encryption for signed documents on the production host
description: Owner decision (counsel where the retention of signed originals is involved). P4-D-7 used a test-only directory; D-45 carried plaintext custody as a limit. For the internal cohort: the storage location under the managed data root, who may retrieve (decision-makers only per P4-D-16), encryption at rest and the key custody strategy (9kg.34 builds it), and the treatment of the provider's copy (P4-D-15) together with POL-10. Authority class: policy. Earliest boundary blocked: 9kg.34 and the go/no-go package. Evidence: the decision in 011 section 4.
acceptance_criteria: The decision recorded in 011 section 4: the custody location, the access rule, the encryption and key-recovery strategy for signed documents on the production host, and the treatment of the provider-held copy; counsel's view on erasure of a jointly signed document (the company's own record is also the subject's) recorded; 9kg.34 implements exactly that.
notes:
Roles: implementer the owner (with counsel where the description says so); reviewer catalyst-independent-qa (the record is traceable and complete); approver: the owner.
Council 2026-10-23 (030 Q4, D-51, provisional): custody under the managed data root, decision-makers only, encrypted with recoverable keys held outside the application backup's rollback domain; encryption before the Documenso canary. The code (9kg.34) is built now; this decision gates the first real submission.

description: Outcome: readiness is shown by real use, not by the deployment succeeding. Steps: the owner (then each cohort member) completes the journey through the public pages and staff screens with no SSH or SQL; each enabled capability's first real effect is checked against its provider read; the representative scenarios of 029 section 8 that are safe on live colleagues (duplicate submission, expired link, partial reply, autoresponder, staff takeover, hold) are exercised with controlled accounts; dangerous fault and rollback drills stay isolated (never injected into colleagues' access); blocked journeys, duplicate effects, support burden, failed communications, security events and recovery time are counted against the abort thresholds; the stop or pause path is tested once. Authority class: real-data action within the launch. Earliest boundary blocked: the wider-enrollment decision. Acceptance: a scenario record with outcomes; no participant record in the repository. Evidence: private record; a PII-free summary in the launch AAR.
acceptance_criteria: a scenario record with outcomes; no participant record in the repository.
notes: Roles: implementer the owner and the cohort (normal paths); reviewer catalyst-independent-qa (the scenario record); approver: the owner.

The authorized preflight step of the launch, not a second pilot service: the force-command verifies the attestation, the stack serves on its unix socket with no route from Learn or any host, every outward kind is held (staging_check.sh's TEST-P6-27 shape, run against the production stack), /readyz green at the exact commit, the nightly backup and its receipt run once, the health timer and sweep alert and recover, the restore drill runs from the production archive into a disposable container. Roles: implementer the owner, or Claude Code only under a recorded go; reviewer catalyst-release-operations; approver: the owner.

For dogfooding: (a) whether an internal participant who already has a company mailbox and signed agreements goes through provisioning at all, is recorded through the checklist fallback as already provisioned, or is excluded from the mailbox step (v2 refuses to adopt an existing account, P5-D-5 and P5-D-10, so the default is a staff item, never a second mailbox); (b) whether withdrawal drills may touch any existing member's access (recommended: never; drills use throwaway accounts only); (c) whether the welcome text and any CRM or community step is a manual handoff with a named owner. Authority class: policy. Earliest boundary blocked: the launch manifest. Evidence: decision in 011 section 4.
acceptance_criteria: The decision recorded in 011 section 4: how an existing member with a mailbox, agreements or a first-generation case takes part (a), the rule that drills never touch an existing member's access (b), and the named owner of the welcome text and any manual handoff (c).

Roles: implementer the owner (with counsel where the description says so); reviewer catalyst-independent-qa (the record is traceable and complete); approver: the owner.
Carries U8 (029 section 12): the existing-member population (who already holds a mailbox, signed agreements or a first-generation case) is the owner's private roster; only aggregate counts enter any record, and the decision names how each existing member takes part.

Council 2026-10-23 (030 Q5, D-51): D-F is a fixed rule, not a provisional value: provisioning disabled, no drill touches an existing mailbox, and the provisioning credential is not present on the host (enforced at host preparation); 9kg.31.3 closes as 'not enabled'. Existing members take part under the per-member 'on file' record of 211.7.4.

title: Verify and complete the recorded human-only assessment path so the internal launch can run with model advice disabled (019 decision 4, P3-D-10 amendment)
description: Outcome: with model requests disabled, a case leaves assessing through a recorded human assessment against the same criteria and snapshot, and the decision names the policy and that no model advice was used. Steps: confirm what 3B.4 built (oc4.10 finding 3 says a human-only decision records no pack or rubric when a policy is set), fix the gap, give staff the capped-snapshot exit (oc4.8 decision) through a screen, and label the dossier. Model output stays nonbinding and disabled during the internal exercise; internal dogfooding is not evidence of selection validity and must not be used for covert staff appraisal (participants are told what is recorded and sent externally). Authority class: repo-only; the policy amendment is the owner's (recorded under 011 section 11). Earliest boundary blocked: the internal launch if any internal participant reaches the decision stage. Acceptance: tests for the human-only path with policy and snapshot recorded; the oc4.10 items (1) to (3) fixed or explicitly deferred. Evidence: CI tests.

notes:
2026-10-23 QA finding 6: the hard edge on the oc4.8 decision removed; this bead builds the staff close-assessment path on the recommended default (route a capped snapshot to a recorded human-only assessment, 019 decision 4) and records that default, so the owner's oc4.8 decision can change the value without redesign.
Roles: implementer Claude Code in a released handoff; reviewer catalyst-minimax-evaluation; approver: the owner.

title: Record ownership of every live first-generation case, mailbox poller, agreement envelope, webhook target and timer, and prove the internal cohort touches none of them
